Mapping the developing group to 'upper_middle' is the extractor's inference: authors say 'only upper-income developing countries' (p.118) but Table 2 includes India, Indonesia, Philippines, Egypt; low income excluded as stated. Group labels are IMF developed/developing, not World Bank bands.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: country/year effects, first differences and a 2SLS check, but instruments (lagged labour hours, PC average selling price) are weakly justified, no first-stage reported, and the Hausman test is non-significant, so exogeneity is not established (moderate).
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: hardware (plus data-communications) spending deflated with a single US quality-adjusted index and depreciated by assumed rates only partly captures IT use.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 45 countries chosen by IT-spending data availability, no low-income country, Korea/Taiwan classed developed (note 4), 14-year panel.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: GDP from PWT 6.3 is output rather than productivity; capital stock extended 2005-2007 with assumed 5% depreciation and regional-average labour hours imputed.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: several estimators, interaction models one at a time, first differences after unit-root tests with FDI/Int/Cel in levels, no multiplicity adjustment.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: main tables show all samples and estimators, but per-capita and Dewan-Kraemer-subsample checks are only 'available upon request' (note 7) and Figure 2 has no numbers.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard cross-country panel with reasonable controls and a modest IV check but exogeneity not established, so moderate is appropriate.

problems: No invented numbers or paper mix-ups found. Table-internal oddities noted by the extractor are real: Table 4 columns FE/2D/RE order is as recorded; Table 7 βK printed '0.3639***'; Table 8 developed Internet βIT SE printed (0.003); Table 6 immigration N = 283 and 51 do not match 219/338 in Table 4. The stronger developing-country effect is not statistically supported (chi2 = 0.34). Minor: the record's n_specifications (~40) is an estimate, not stated in the paper; 2D-cluster-SE columns in Table 4 (0.150*** (0.040), 0.137** (0.044), 0.103* (0.053)) are not in results but not misreported.
